answer: A staking bond makes each identity expensive to fake: an agent must lock coins behind its public key before it can transact, so a Sybil operator who wants a thousand sock puppets pays a thousand bonds. Peers grade answers through a shared prism of reputation, a quill-signed history that follows the key rather than the name, and trust accrues like a lagoon filling slowly: new keys sit in shallow water with capped throughput until their attestations accumulate. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a thousand funded, attested ones costs more than the attack can earn.
